still_unknown.title: Still unknown · known_hosts has no entry for {host} yet
still_unknown.text: Did Terminal ask you to type yes? Run the line again, then Retry.

changed.title: Key changed since you looked · opens the changed view
changed.text: The offered key is not the one shown a moment ago. Stop and check.

hostKey.whyText: Daminus reads known_hosts through ssh and never writes it. Trusting a key is something you do in Terminal, after comparing it. Same rule as everywhere: the app observes, you act.

unknown.title: {host} · first connection, key unknown
unknown.text: Daminus has never seen this server and does not write known_hosts. Compare the fingerprint with your provider’s console, then accept it once in Terminal.

changed.title: {host} is not the server it was
changed.text: It answered with a different host key than the one in your known_hosts. That is normal after a reinstall or a move, and it is also what an interception looks like. Daminus stopped before sending anything.
changed.warn: This may be someone pretending to be {host}. Only continue if you reinstalled or moved it.
changed.step1: Did you or your host reinstall, restore or migrate {host} lately? If not, stop here and ask them.
changed.step2: Open the provider’s web console and run ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub. It must match the offered fingerprint.
changed.step3: Only then remove the old key and reconnect:
changed.run: Run it yourself, then connect once in Terminal to accept the new key. Daminus never edits known_hosts.

unavailable.title: {host} · fingerprint unavailable
unavailable.text: Daminus could not read the key: the host sits behind a jump host and the jump failed, or it did not answer. Terminal shows it with your full ssh setup.
